what: Frame cost of the set designer's sets on a Meta Quest 3S in the Quest Browser, measured on 14 November 2026 in an immersive session on the development server, build bcc6e32 (with the limit of things a reply may hold still at 40). Each set was replayed from a saved designer reply (no model was called), with the same page code as the emulator runs (tmp/t-perf.mjs through tmp/q-perf-sets.py): three seconds idle, three seconds with one piece moved every frame, and the build itself. Both hands were tracked throughout. The budget at 90 Hz is 11.1 ms a frame; the competition's floor is 60 fps (16.7 ms).

second_run_hands_open.condition: Hands held open above the table edge, not touching or pointing at pieces.

gas_station.note: Frame intervals not used: the session logger's own frame sampling ran during these seconds and split them.

first_run_hands_pointing.condition: Hands pointing at the set; at times they closed on pieces and carried them, so 'moving' includes real carrying. The funeral and the gas station were refused (a piece was held) and are left out.

found: Sets the real model writes (6 to 14 pieces, up to 6 made) held 87 to 89 fps standing (90 stepped inside) and 71 to 83 with a piece moving.
No shader was compiled while any set was built: the warm-up at the start of the session had made all 104 programs.
40 things at once fell to 49 fps with a piece moving, and 24 ran 63 to 64; the limit of things in one reply is lowered to 20 in the next build.
